**Root cause (confirmed, systematic).** The GCP smoke crashed at the reused #825 extractor's `causal_check` on the NEW early-position `prefix` slot (`s0:prefix layer 0`, max|diff|=0.03125 instruct / 0.0625 pretrained). Diagnosis walked the brief's three hypotheses in order:

1. **Random-projection control misused as prefix-degeneracy evidence.** Result 5: "within-R² 0.12–0.13, above the ~−0.004 null but matching a dimension-matched random-projection control." The control (`random_projection_control` in `issue825_fit_cells.py:329` — X→X@P, P full-rank Gaussian) preserves all linear information by construction, so it matches the observed R² in EVERY cell, including the headline context cells (instruct chat: control 0.6502 vs observed 0.6542; base r2: 0.5717 vs 0.5783 — `cells_R_*_context.json` `random_projection_control_r2`). Matching it therefore carries zero degeneracy information; by the body's implied logic the context arm would be "degenerate" too. Ground the prefix-weakness claim on the 0.13-vs-0.65 gap + the near-constant-prefix variance instead, and either drop the control comparison or state what it actually is (a feature-scramble pipeline sanity check that matches everywhere). — suggested weakening: delete "but matching a dimension-matched random-projection control" or replace with the variance argument.

VERBATIM USER ASK: "is ARIA named aria in the stories or 'assistant'? could you rerun with a character named 'assistant'?"

## Follow-up goal
Disentangle a NAME effect from a FRAMING effect in the R3 story-collapse result. The #1345 story arm named the AI character "ARIA" (a novel proper name; STORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT: "an AI assistant named ARIA", attribution `ARIA replied: "..."`), and the assistant map collapsed there (context R² −0.754 @ L19, instruct). That could be because the character has an UNFAMILIAR NAME (the assistant map isn't tied to "ARIA") rather than because it's narrative-story FRAMING. Rerun the story arm with the character literally named **"Assistant"** and re-test.

## Design (single manipulated variable = the character name)
- IDENTICAL to the #1345 R3 story arm in every respect EXCEPT the character's name: replace "ARIA" with **"Assistant"** throughout `STORY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` and the attribution template (`Assistant replied: "..."` — or the nearest natural-prose form; the extraction slot = the last token of the attribution marker immediately before the Assistant's quoted answer, exactly as the ARIA arm extracted at `ARIA replied:`).
- Same on-policy generation (elicitation tier 2, instruct-and-strip; the story-writing system instruction is NOT part of the extracted context), same judge-filter (≥4 well-formed Q→A exchanges), same per-turn confidence gate, same yield floor (400) + retry budget.
- INSTRUCT is the primary arm (the #1345 base story arm was below the yield floor, 96/500 — retry base only if it clears the floor this time; otherwise report base N/A again).
- Fit the story map (context→answer, + prefix arm), sweep 28 layers within-regime, and re-run the SAME comparison legs vs the (unchanged) chat + no-template maps: within-regime held-out R² + shuffle null; cross-regime transfer (Assistant-story ↔ chat/no-template); raw + rotation-aligned operator cosine; and the general-linear reparameterization (does A·M·B recover a target ceiling?).

## Reads / what would answer it
- **Name effect:** if the "Assistant"-named story map EXISTS (within-regime R² positive, above the mean baseline) and/or transfers to / reparameterizes onto the chat operator, then the ARIA collapse was largely a name/familiarity effect — the map IS tied to the literal "assistant" identity.
- **Framing effect:** if the "Assistant"-named story map ALSO collapses (context R² near/below the ARIA −0.754, below the answer-mean baseline), then the collapse is the narrative-prose FRAMING, not the name — the map is tied to the conversational assistant TURN, independent of what the character is called. Either outcome sharpens #1345 Result 2.

## Standing rules to carry
- Prefix mapping AND context mapping BOTH arms (per the standing rule).
- Layer-19 headline + full 28-layer sweep; conversation/story-grouped held-out CV; shuffle null per regime/cell.
- On-policy generation; data-realism + on-policy-completions elicitation ladder; report yield + drops.
- Corpus caveat carried forward: stories are a different corpus than the LMSYS chat/no-template conversations (corpus-confounded by design); this rerun changes ONLY the character name, so it is a clean within-story-corpus name manipulation.
- REUSE the #1345 story machinery verbatim (issue1345_gen_stories.py / issue1345_common.py / the fit + transfer + operator-comparison legs) — only the character-name constant changes. Vectorize fits.

## Headline read

**The registered verdict lattice (plan v9 §3) fires FRAMING EFFECT.** The paired-verbatim story within-regime context-arm R² at layer 19 (instruct) is **−0.306** (bootstrap-rig −0.303; conversation-grouped 1,000-draw bootstrap 95% CI **[−0.332, −0.279]**, n=2,163 conversations) — wholly below zero — while on the SAME 2,163 conversations with the SAME answer text the chat map reads **+0.243** [0.224, 0.266]. The collapse is not the corpus: same conversations, same answers, matched n, and the narrative framing still destroys the context→answer map. Per conversation, the story map's relative error exceeds the chat map's for **88.0%** of the 2,163 shared conversations (median relative error 1.27 story vs 0.78 chat). The story map remains above its shuffle null (p95 −2.01) — a map "exists" — but it predicts worse than the test-fold answer mean at every one of the 28 layers (best −0.306 at L19).

**Same-rows comparator surprise (reported, not headline):** the story-kept subset is not innocuous. Chat drops 0.654→0.243 and plain-text drops 0.625→**0.019** [−0.010, 0.050] under the same 2,163-row restriction (selection favors short, verbatim-embeddable answers ≤800 tokens; n also halves). The framing gradient on identical rows is story −0.306 < plain-text 0.019 < chat 0.243; the registered verdict rests only on the story CI being wholly below zero while the chat comparator stays positive on the same rows.

**TF tier-1 qualification (mandatory carry):** on the 117-conversation on-policy companion subset, the teacher-forced story cell reads **+0.069** [0.053, 0.139] vs the on-policy companion's **−0.006** [−0.008, 0.055]: gap **+0.075** > the 0.05 qualification band, < the 0.20 kill gate → the TF headline stands with the companion read attached (plan v8/v9 §7 nested tiers; the gap also bundles any residual pre-slot construction inflation per the calibration note). Direction: TF *inflates* the story read, so the on-policy story map would be weaker still — the framing-effect verdict is robust to the qualification. Prefix arm shows no TF inflation (TF-on-companion −0.202 vs companion −0.212).

## The localization insight (new this round)

The data-paired reparameterization leg — now DEFINED because story rows share conversation ids with chat — is **one-way**:

- **Story→chat recovers fully:** `A·M_story·B` evaluated in chat reads **0.610**, above the matched chat ceiling 0.243 (matched-capacity null −0.040; margin-adjusted delta +0.417). The regularized composition through the story operator out-generalizes the direct chat fit at this n, as the parent saw for the no-template composition.
- **Chat→story fails:** recovery reads **−0.172**, below even the matched-capacity null (−0.060; delta −0.111). Nothing linear predicts the story answer-mean activations from the story context slot at better than fold-mean level.
- **The failure is localized to the story CONTEXT representation:** a direct ridge fit from the *chat* context activations to the *story* answer activations of the same conversations reads **0.561** (battery `repswap_i2b`) — the story ANSWER representation retains the predictable structure; the story context slot (last token of `Assistant replied: "`) is the deficient object. Conversely the story context cannot predict even the chat answers (−0.309, `repswap_b2i`).
- **Operator similarity is mid-band:** data-paired activation-Procrustes aligned cosine **0.455** (raw 0.026; rotation null p97.5 ≈ 0.0005; 50 draws) vs the chat↔plain-text pair's 0.855 aligned / 0.651 raw; top-10 principal-angle mean cosine 0.736 vs 0.987.

Naive story↔chat transfer collapses in all four directions (−2.7 to −3.7 context-arm R², each above its own shuffle null). Prefix arm concurs everywhere: story prefix within −1.371 [−1.432, −1.310] (genuine narrative text, NOT the fixed-template degeneracy of the chat/plain-text prefix ≈0.13); story→chat prefix reparam barely clears (delta +0.050), chat→story fails (−0.075).

Interpretation (labeled as such): the story context activation looks like chat-equivalent signal plus large framing-specific variability; errors-in-variables attenuation then kills the within-story fit while the operator's shared structure survives — consistent with one assistant operator whose story-side input coordinates are unstable, and NOT with a wholly different story operator (that would not reparameterize into chat above capacity nulls).

## The localization insight (new this round)

The data-paired reparameterization leg — now DEFINED because story rows share conversation ids with chat — is **one-way**:

- **Story→chat recovers fully:** `A·M_story·B` evaluated in chat reads **0.610**, above the matched chat ceiling 0.243 (matched-capacity null −0.040; margin-adjusted delta +0.417). - **Chat→story fails:** recovery reads **−0.172**, below even the matched-capacity null (−0.060; delta −0.111). Nothing linear predicts the story answer-mean activations from the story context slot at better than fold-mean level.
- **The failure is localized to the story CONTEXT representation:** a direct ridge fit from the *chat* context activations to the *story* answer activations of the same conversations reads **0.561** (battery `repswap_i2b`) — above even the matched chat ceiling 0.243, so the story ANSWER is the easier target and retains the predictable structure; the story context slot (last token of `Assistant replied: "`) is the deficient object.
